subject: Animation
title: How Pixar Storyboards a Film
description: A quick win: understand How Pixar Storyboards a Film.

hook.text: Before a single frame is animated, Pixar draws the entire film as thousands of storyboard sketches.

buildup.text: These rough drawings are edited into an animatic — a filmed version of the storyboard with temp voices.

discovery.text: The animatic lets directors screen the entire movie cheaply and find story problems before production.

twist.text: A typical Pixar film goes through six to ten complete storyboard passes before animation even begins.

climax.text: This process is slow and expensive, but it ensures that story problems are solved on paper, not pixels.

punchline.text: Pixar perfects the film in pencil before touching a computer.

quiz.question: Why does Pixar storyboard so extensively before animating?
options: To reduce the number of voice actors needed
To find and fix story problems cheaply before expensive animation production begins
To create promotional material for marketing

details.summary: Pixar storyboards every film extensively before any animation begins, creating thousands of drawings that function as a rough visual draft. This process reveals story problems cheaply in drawings rather than expensively in finished animation.
details.whyItMatters: Storyboarding is Pixar's most cost-effective creative tool. By testing every story beat as a sketch before committing resources to animation, they catch problems when fixes cost pennies rather than millions.
takeaways: Pixar creates thousands of storyboard drawings before animating each film
Storyboards function as cheap, early drafts that reveal story problems
Finding problems in drawings saves millions compared to fixing finished animation

faq.question: How many storyboard drawings does a typical Pixar film require?
faq.answer: A typical Pixar film goes through 75,000 to 100,000 individual storyboard drawings. Most are discarded as sequences are reworked. The final film might represent a fraction of the total drawings produced, but each discarded sketch helped find the right version.

faq.question: What happens during a Pixar story pitch?
faq.answer: Artists pin storyboards to a wall and perform the sequence — acting out dialogue, creating sound effects, controlling pacing. It is theatrical performance using drawings. The audience experiences the story's emotional beats before a single frame is animated.
